classification.difficultyReason: Form and solve an angle-sum equation from three expressions, substitute the parameter, and justify the isosceles classification using equal angles.

content.prompt: Show that this triangle is isosceles.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle with horizontal base, upper apex, and interior angle arcs. Algebraic labels retain their source vertices; drawing proportions are schematic.
spec.mathematics: Left base angle (3a+29)°, apex angle (4a+16)°, right base angle (4a−8)°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied expressions are visible; evaluated angles are answer content.

answer.short: $a=13$. The angles are $68^{\circ},68^{\circ},44^{\circ}$, so the triangle is isosceles.
answer.worked:
Angles in a triangle sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}(3a+29)+(4a+16)+(4a-8)&=180\\11a+37&=180\\11a&=143\\a&=13\end{align*}$$
Substituting gives $3(13)+29=68$, $4(13)+16=68$ and $4(13)-8=44$. Two angles are equal, so the triangle is isosceles.
